Consult Summary:
- A 53-year-old man presents with about one week of a left elbow swelling that is warm but not painful; exam suggests bursitis rather than septic arthritis.
- Plan includes NSAID therapy and blood tests to evaluate inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic causes, with follow-up to review results; instructions provided for potential urgent evaluation if symptoms worsen.

Problem List:

Issue 1:
- Left elbow swelling for ~1 week; warmth around the area; the patient can move the elbow normally and reports no significant pain or injury.
- Exam findings: left elbow swelling, skin warmth, dry skin at the tip of the elbow, no marked tenderness on palpation away from swelling; patient able to raise elbow; no obvious signs of septic arthritis.
- Assessment/differential: suspected elbow bursitis; septic arthritis not currently suspected.
- Social history/medications/examination findings: desk-based job; participates in running 2–3 times per week; allergic to peanuts; no regular medications.
- Specialist/allied health review/differential diagnosis: planned blood tests to exclude inflammatory/infectious/rheumatologic causes (inflammatory markers, infection screening, rheumatologic antibodies, gout).

Issue 2:
- Investigations planned: blood tests to screen for inflammatory markers, infection, rheumatologic antibodies, and gout; forms to be mailed with instructions.
- Timeline: results expected in about 5–6 days after testing; follow-up appointment arranged to review results.

Issue 3:
- History of osteoarthritis (self-reported; diagnosed by GP a few years ago) with intermittent joint pain; no formal rheumatology confirmation noted in current encounter.

Medications:
- Ibuprofen 400 mg; route not documented; frequency: twice daily; take after meals. (Note: heartburn caution; discontinue if symptoms occur.)

Allergies:
- Peanut allergy.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis (self-reported; diagnosed by GP in the past).
- No other illnesses reported; no regular medications; no known drug allergies besides peanut allergy.

Social History:
- Employment: desk-based work; physically active with running 2–3 times per week.
- No smoking or alcohol details provided.

Preventative History:
- Not documented.

Physical Examination:
- Left elbow swelling with warmth; ability to move the elbow; no focal tenderness beyond swelling; skin around elbow tip described as dry; no signs of septic arthritis observed during exam.

Plan:
- Initiate ibuprofen 400 mg by mouth twice daily after meals; discontinue if heartburn occurs.
- Send blood test forms to patient’s home for:
  - Inflammatory markers
  - Infection screening
  - Rheumatologic antibodies
  - Gout evaluation
- Follow-up appointment to review blood test results and reassess the elbow; follow-up can be in-person, telehealth, or video, at patient’s preference.
- Instruct patient to seek urgent care (phone/video appointment) if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads or worsens (emergency sign).

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs, imaging results (none obtained), explicit ROS details beyond elbow symptoms, and complete vaccination history not documented.
- Internal conflicts: none identified; transcript supports bursitis impression with no current septic arthritis.
- Transcript quality: generally clear; contains some informal/repetitive phrasing and filler words. No irreconcilable inconsistencies.
